Subject: Cloud reserve backstop proposal for Acme AI / DEAL-1429

Karthik / Ben —

Following our call yesterday, attached is a short reserve offer that would serve as an operational backstop while OEM lead times firm up. High level: a 6-month committed reserve for up to 120 vGPUs (H100-equivalent), with an option to convert to dedicated on-prem inventory should Acme proceed. We can stage the commitment in three monthly tranches to match their onboarding cadence.

Key things I want to surface now:
- We can guarantee warm capacity in region us-west-2 within 7 business days for the first tranche (40 vGPUs) if PO and billing are in place.
- Longer-term 90–120 day fulfillment for the full 120 vGPU pool if they want a reserved capacity discount.
- Pricing and SKU mapping are in the attached CloudScale-reserve-offer-20280414.xlsx; it's intentionally conservative on utilization.

If you can confirm what exact SKU mix Acme is asking for (A100 vs H100 equivalency / memory-per-instance), I can firm the numbers. Also open to signing a short-term bridging agreement with partial billing to accelerate the first shipment.

Thanks —
Samir
Enterprise Sales, CloudScale EMEA

Samir — thanks, this is helpful.

Couple of asks so we can make a combined recommendation to Acme this week:
1) Alicia / Orion — we need your updated OEM quote (line-item SKUs + per-unit ETA). Ben mentioned Orion could front-load 20 units for quicker integration testing; can you confirm whether partial shipments are possible and the earliest ship date? Please attach the formal quote.
2) Samir — confirm the convertibility terms (what is the conversion fee to on-prem dedicated units and the runway to convert?). Also please call out how quickly CloudScale can expand warm capacity beyond the first tranche if the customer accelerates.
3) Internal — Ben / Marissa, Acme wants a firm go/no-go by 2028-04-22 for the first tranche (40 units) to meet their product ETA. I want us to propose a hybrid cadence: 20 on-prem (OEM), 20 cloud-warm (reserve) for month one, then tranche 2 (40) in month two, tranche 3 (40) in month three. This keeps their latency-critical use on dedicated hardware while we use cloud as a safety valve.

I've attached the Orion quote we received on 2028-04-10 for reference (Orion_quote_20280410.pdf). Ben / Marissa — can you check margin sensitivity on the staged funding model and whether finance can accept a split PO model?

Karthik
Director, Deals

Karthik —

Appreciate the clear plan. Attached is an updated quote with two fulfillment options:
A) Standard queue — full build and delivery in 10–12 weeks for the requested configuration (80 x H100-like blades, full warranty)
B) Staged ship — we can push 20 units to ship in 6 weeks (partial configuration — power-cage and baseboard ready) with the balance shipped in week 10. There is a modest premium for staged packing and expedited test cycles.

Notes:
- We can hold a small inventory buffer for Redwood deals if you commit to a minimum 6-month warranty extension and a partial deposit.
- We do not tie inventory to specific customer POs without a conversion agreement; conversion from reserve to dedicated unit requires an RMA/assignment document (I attached sample language).

Attachment: Orion_quote_20280410.pdf

If you want, I can set up a quick call tomorrow to walk pricing and lead-time tradeoffs tied to your deal milestones.

Best,
Alicia Gomez
Head of Sales Engineering, Orion Systems

Subject: Final MAP & next steps for procurement cadence (DEAL-1429)

Team / Acme —

Putting the mutual action plan (MAP) in writing so everyone is aligned. I've attached a short doc (MutualActionPlan_DEAL-1429_v1.docx) with the same bullets. Key milestones:
1) 2028-04-22 — Acme internal approval (go/no-go) for tranche 1 (40 units) — action: Acme procurement to sign PO or advise conversion to CloudScale reserve by EOD 22nd.
2) 2028-04-25 — Redwood to issue split PO draft + deposit instruction (Ben).
3) 2028-04-28 — Orion to confirm earliest ship date for the 20-unit partial release and provide tracking.
4) 2028-05-05 — Standup integration window for the first tranche (Redwood infra + Acme test plan).

Contingency plan: if Orion cannot meet the 6-week partial ship, CloudScale will provide the first 40 warm vGPUs within 7 business days; conversion terms will be as per Samir's attachment.

Open items for Acme procurement: confirm exact SKU memory profile and whether they require full H100 pass-through (this impacts OS image sizing and kernel tuning). Also we need the signed conversion language if they intend to convert CloudScale reserve to dedicated units later.

I'll book the internal signoff meeting for Tue 10:00 PT and send meeting notes afterwards.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Onboarding
